content.overview: Vicarious liability makes one person answerable for the tort of another because of a relationship (typically employer-employee) and a connection between the tort and the relationship (course of employment). It is not a substitute for proving the underlying tort of the wrongdoer.

sections.heading: Employer and employee
sections.body: Identify a contract of service (control and integration tests as guides). The tort must occur in the course of employment — authorised acts and wrongful modes of doing authorised acts may attract liability; a frolic of one's own may not.

sections.heading: Independent contractors
sections.body: Ordinarily the employer is not vicariously liable for an independent contractor, subject to non-delegable duties and hazardous operations exceptions.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead the employee's tort and the employment nexus. Join employer and employee where appropriate. Evidence: appointment, duties, time and place of the act, and benefit to the employer's enterprise.
